plan.title: feat(scope): one-PR path for a single maintainer: a new or widened brief lands with its code without a second human reviewer

narratives.Description: A single maintainer cannot land a new or widened brief together with its code in one PR, because membership trusts file_scope only from the merge base and the #6203 path needs a second human reviewer. This story adds an owner-chosen proof level, plan.policy.onePrScopeProof (off by default, mint, signed), read from the merge base together with requireHumanMerge. At the mint level, the existing human-presence mint stamps the head brief auth-hash, the record rides in the same PR, and verify:scope-provenance admits it only on an exact scope match and prints the admitted scope with the line that CI cannot tell a real mint from a forged one. The signed level is deferred to #5862.
narratives.Overview:
1. Policy level: `plan.policy.onePrScopeProof` with values `off` (default), `mint`, `signed`. It is read together with `plan.policy.requireHumanMerge` from the merge base (`git show <merge-base>:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`), never from the head. A PR that changes either field cannot use the one-PR path. Setter: `deft policy:set-one-pr-scope-proof -- --set off|mint --confirm`, in the shape of the existing policy setters. `signed` is reserved and the setter refuses it with a pointer to #5862 until that story lands.
2. Mint level: admitted only when the merge-base level is `mint` and merge-base `requireHumanMerge` is true. `scope:record-approved-scope` (unchanged human-presence gate) also stamps `authHashV1`, the head brief's auth-hash v1 (`computeAuthHashV1`), into the record. The `self-authorizing-scope-expansion` guard admits a same-PR `.deft/approved-scope/<id>.json` (and its `.intent.json`) only under that level, and only when all of these hold: the record's `authHashV1` equals the head brief's auth-hash; the record's `planId` and `xbriefRelPath` match the head brief; the record's normalized `fileScope` equals the head brief's normalized `file_scope` exactly and its `fileScopeDigest` matches that list; the head brief's `file_scope` has no glob entry (concrete-only, like `forge-approval`); and `isHumanApprovalStamp` passes. Membership then uses that record as `mint` authority. In every other case the guard is unchanged.
3. Visibility: on a mint-level admit, `verify:scope-provenance` prints the plan id, the admitted `file_scope`, the production-file count and the line "CI cannot tell this mint from a file an agent wrote; the human merge is the control". It appends the same block to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` when that variable is set.
4. Unchanged: the #4956 production fence (merge-base only), Path B, the separate mint-record PR, #6203 forge approval, and `requireHumanMerge` semantics.
5. Docs: `docs/scope-provenance.md` names the three levels, says the mint level is a human-merge trust anchor that CI cannot verify (the same anchor as today's record PR), says a bot-merge repo cannot use it, and keeps the earlier lean's non-goals (#6207, #4956).
6. Tests: mint level with `requireHumanMerge` true and a matching `authHashV1` admits a new brief and a widened-past-mint brief in one change set; the same with `requireHumanMerge` false is refused; a level set only in the head is refused; an `authHashV1` that differs from the head brief is refused; a record whose `fileScope` differs from the head brief (with a matching hash) is refused; a glob added to the head brief after the mint is refused; head brief drift after the mint is refused; the valid case runs with both the `.json` and `.intent.json` in the changed-file set and in the declared scope; level `off` (and an absent field) gives today's behaviour; the setter refuses `signed`; the step-summary block is written when `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is set.
narratives.UserStory: As a repo owner who keeps requireHumanMerge on, I want to opt in to a mint proof level for one-PR scope, so that a new or widened brief, its human mint record and its code land in one PR without a second reviewer.

- Infer the level from the PR head, from forge collaborator counts, or from PR-authored config.
- Allow the mint level in a repo where `requireHumanMerge` is false (bot merge).
- Claim the mint level proves human presence to CI; the docs and the CI line say it does not.
- Build the signed level in this story (deferred to #5862, design input lean 6856783754).
- Let either level widen the #4956 production fence.

## In plain English
A single maintainer cannot land a new or widened brief together with its code in one PR. Membership trusts `file_scope` only from the merge base, and the one-PR path from #6203 needs an approving review from a second person, which GitHub never lets an author give. The open question is what proof a single human can put in the same PR that CI can tell apart from a file the agent wrote, given that the agent uses the operator's own forge identity (#6207).

## Pains
- P1 — A new or widened brief costs a separate brief or record PR before its code PR (two to four PRs per change, each with review, pre-PR run and merge).
- P2 — The #6203 one-PR proof needs an APPROVED review by a non-author with repo write; one human with one forge identity can never produce it.
- P3 — On a solo setup the agent acts under the operator's forge identity, so any forge-side or in-tree proof is something the agent could also produce (#6207). No proof exists today that CI can check and that only the human can produce.

## In plain English

One PR is feasible, but the existing typed mint does not give CI verifiable evidence of human presence. The design needs an approval capability the agent cannot exercise, plus a verifier and trusted key configuration the PR cannot replace. A signature alone solves neither requirement. Bind the proposal only after those trust boundaries and the remaining scope fences are explicit; otherwise its acceptance criteria promise more than the mechanism delivers.

### 1. blocks-the-design — The existing mint is a local guard, not portable human-presence proof

**Evidence:** At pinned SHA `1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04`, `packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts:194–269` checks environment markers, terminal availability, `--confirm`, and a fixed phrase. `packages/runtime/src/authz.ts:817–833` invokes that guard before minting. `packages/core/src/authz/store.ts:866–878` constructs an ordinary `operator-cli` origin object. Its threat model expressly excludes credential-compromised local-file forgery (`packages/core/src/authz/types.ts:1–7`).

The approved-scope record similarly contains hashes and optional provenance fields, not a signature (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/digest.ts:142–161`); its human-stamp predicate recognizes strings (`225–245`). `mint-artifacts.ts:503–535` serializes the record and intent.

**Failure mode:** CI receives identical bytes whether the CLI produced them or an agent fabricated them. Adding a signature under an unreadable key still fails if the agent can invoke an unlocked signing service. An injected worker needs signing access, not key extraction.

**Disposition consequence:** Require **human-gated key use**, not merely key secrecy. The typed CLI may remain a convenience guard, but cannot be the claimed security boundary. Define a supported signer whose approval path lies outside agent control, including per-request confirmation of the actual scope.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The trusted verifier and key enrollment must be outside the candidate’s authority

**Evidence:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:150–193` checks out the candidate, installs dependencies, materializes the runtime from that tree, and executes `task check:merge`. This is useful dogfooding, but not independent verification against hostile candidate code. Existing pre-PR HMAC machinery (`packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/store.ts:113–125`) provides local integrity checking; it does not establish an operator-only signer.

CI then has to tell a human's approval apart from a file the agent wrote, and on a solo setup the agent uses the human's own GitHub identity and OS account. Its first key candidate, "a key the agent cannot read", tests the wrong thing: the agent does not need to read a key, only use it. The thinnest sound mechanism I can find is a signature that needs a physical touch on a security key. The public key is pinned on the merge base, which also makes it the opt-in. The design can bind once its proof clause is restated that way.

### 1. The named trust anchor is not a proof CI can observe (blocks-the-design)
Evidence: `packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts` lines 1–8, 17–60 and 135–156. The gate checks TTY, opens a controlling terminal, reads a typed `mint`, and refuses on an env-var denylist (`CLAUDECODE`, `CI`, …). The output is a JSON record. `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/digest.ts` lines 30–35 and 226–246 show that `humanApproval` is free-form strings, and `isHumanApprovalStamp` accepts any `kind` in a string set (`"cli"`, `"operator"`, …). Today that record gets its authority only from being on the merge base, not from its content (`evaluate.ts` 1141–1178, 1159–1178).
Failure mode: an agent writes `{"humanApproval":{"kind":"cli","actor":"scott",…}}` directly, or runs the CLI under `env -u CLAUDECODE` with an allocated PTY. CI sees a file that cannot be told apart from a real mint. The local gate guards against accidental agent use, not against an injected agent, and CI never sees it run.
Disposition: Expected bullet 2 and the Constraint must change "human-presence mint bound to the auth-hash" to "an asymmetric signature over the auth-hash, under a merge-base-pinned key whose every use needs physical presence". `authz:grant`-style TTY ceremony may stay as UX but carries no authority.

That is the env denylist above, plus shell-pattern denial of writes to `.deft/authz/grants/` (`packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` ~279–534 and its tests at `classify.test.ts` 511–656, a long pattern list per binary). Failure mode: the agent runs as the operator's OS user. A software key loaded in `ssh-agent`, `gpg-agent` with a cached passphrase, or an OS keyring without a per-use prompt signs any payload for any same-user process through `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. The agent never reads the key and still gets a valid signature.
Disposition: the requirement is "cannot use without a human physical act". That means a FIDO2 `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` / `sk-ecdsa` key with touch required. CI must refuse non-`sk` key types and signers lines marked `no-touch-required`.

Disposition: do not count `requireHumanMerge` as the second control in the safety case. The signature closes "who approved the scope". Merge identity stays on #6207.

Disposition: make opt-in explicit and reviewed. The path is live only when a signers file exists on the merge base. Landing that file is a team decision through normal review. Do not use live forge collaborator counting, which is mutable and racy.

Sign over a fixed namespace (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -n deft-scope-mint-v1`) plus the origin repo slug plus the auth-hash v1. A git commit signature (namespace `git`) or another repo's attestation then cannot be replayed.

### 9. Touch is not the same as reading (footnote)
If the agent starts `ssh-keygen -Y sign`, the human sees only a blinking key. The mint verb should print the concrete `file_scope` and acceptance preimage, and it should be the human who runs it. What remains is a human touching without reading.

- **Mint (human, local):** `deft scope:sign -- <brief>` shows the preimage, then signs `namespace + repo slug + auth-hash v1` with a FIDO2 `sk` key (touch required). It writes `.deft/scope-attest/<safe-plan-id>.sig`.
- **One fail-closed check** in `verify:scope-provenance`, at the forge-admit site but also under `mint` authority. It recomputes the head auth-hash and runs `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against the merge-base signers with the fixed namespace. It refuses non-`sk` key types and `no-touch-required` lines. On success it admits membership with the head's concrete `file_scope`. Any failure returns today's finding and remediation unchanged.
- **One remediation line:** "sign with your security key (`deft scope:sign`) or land the brief first (Path B)."
- **What the agent cannot do:** produce a valid signature without a touch on a device whose public key is on the merge base, or enrol its own key without a merged signers change.

Split identities per #6207. ## In plain English
Problem: a single maintainer cannot land a new or widened brief together with its code in one PR. Membership trusts `file_scope` only from the merge base, and the #6203 one-PR path needs an approving review from a second person. On a solo setup the agent uses the operator's own GitHub identity and OS account, so a file, a label or a review is not proof of the human.

Solution this lean proposes: a signed scope attestation that claims only what it can prove. The repo opts in by landing an OpenSSH allowed-signers file through normal review, and CI reads it only from the merge base. To approve a brief, the human runs one signing step in their own terminal. It reads the brief from a commit they name (a commit cannot change once named), shows the exact scope (repo, PR, plan id, brief path, concrete `file_scope`, acceptance criteria), asks them to type the plan id, and signs those same in-memory bytes with a touch-required security key. Nothing is read back from the working tree between showing and signing, so swapping a file does not change what gets signed. It then writes the preimage and signature into the PR. CI checks the signature over the committed bytes and checks that those bytes equal the scope it recomputes from the head brief. With a valid signature, membership admits the head brief's scope, both for a new brief and for one widened past an existing mint. Without one, nothing changes.

What it does not claim: protection against an agent that edits the gate code in the same PR, changes repo settings with the shared identity, tampers with the operator's installed tools, or controls what the operator's terminal shows. That stays the #6207 posture. A widening past the #4956 production allowance that cannot split still cannot land in one PR, by #4956's design. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this attestation and those two stated limits. There is no leftover next-build.

## Bound remedy
1. Opt-in and trust pin: an OpenSSH `allowed_signers` file at `.deft/scope-signers`, read only via `git show <merge-base>:`. If it is absent on the merge base, the signed path is off and every current path is unchanged. Only `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` / `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` lines count, `no-touch-required` lines are refused, and `valid-after` / `valid-before` are honoured. Revocation is removing the line on the merge base. A PR that changes `.deft/scope-signers` cannot use the signed path. The key-type check is a configuration guard, not a hardware proof; a human landing each signers line through a reviewed merge is the control.
2. One-process signing, run by the human: `deft scope:sign -- <brief> --pr <N> --commit <sha>` reads the brief with `git show <sha>:<path>`, builds the canonical preimage in memory (namespace `deft-scope-attest-v1`, origin repo slug, PR number, plan id, brief path, concrete `file_scope`, acceptance criteria: the auth-hash v1 fields, readable), prints it, requires the human to type the plan id, then passes those same bytes on stdin to `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n deft-scope-attest-v1 -f <key>`. It writes `.deft/scope-attest/<safe-plan-id>.preimage.json` and the signature from that one buffer. It reads no working-tree file between display and signing. It reuses the human-presence factor checks (TTY, controlling terminal, agent/CI markers) as an accident guard, not as proof.
3. Signature: `.deft/scope-attest/<safe-plan-id>.preimage.json.sig`, outside `.deft/approved-scope/`. The `self-authorizing-scope-expansion` guard is unchanged.
4. One fail-closed check in `verify:scope-provenance`: recompute the canonical preimage from the head brief, repo and PR; require byte equality with the committed preimage; run `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against the merge-base signers with the fixed namespace. On success, admit the head brief's concrete `file_scope` for membership (authority `signed-attestation`, concrete-only like `forge-approval`). It runs where the #6203 forge admit runs and also under `mint` authority. On any failure it returns today's finding plus one remediation line: sign the committed preimage with your security key (`deft scope:sign`), or land the brief first (Path B).
5. Unchanged: the #4956 production fence (merge-base only), Path B, the mint-record PR, #6203 forge approval, and `requireHumanMerge`. The docs state the claim plainly: the signature proves that a human activated an enrolled key over the exact committed scope bytes. It does not prove who merged, and it does not hold against an agent that edits the gate code, the repo settings or the operator's terminal (#6207).
6. Tests: a valid `sk` signature over a matching preimage admits a new brief and a widened-past-mint brief; a stamped `kind:"cli"` record with no signature is refused; a preimage that differs from the head brief by one byte is refused; head brief drift after signing is refused; a non-`sk` key, a `no-touch-required` line, a signers line added in the PR, a wrong namespace, a wrong repo, a wrong PR and an expired line are each refused; an absent signers file gives today's behaviour.

## Summary

Membership (#4774 / #5192) trusts a brief's `file_scope` only from the merge base. A new or widened brief therefore needs its own PR before the code PR, or a minted approved-scope record that itself lands on master in a separate record PR. #6203 (0.129.7) added a one-PR path, but its only proof is a GitHub APPROVED review by a **non-author** user with write access (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/forge-approval.ts`). GitHub does not let an author approve their own PR, so a single maintainer can never use it.

A single maintainer is the common consumer shape. For them every brief change still costs two or three PRs (brief or record, code, completion), each with its own review, pre-PR run and merge.

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, one change needed four PRs: brief, record, implementation and completion. The record PR alone (a mint after a clause rebinding) cost a full review, pre-PR run and merge cycle. The maintainer of this repo has the same problem on solo work.

## Constraint

On a solo setup the agent acts under the operator's own forge identity. Any forge-side proof (a review, a label, an environment approval, a comment) is something the agent could produce too; that is the #6207 confused-deputy posture, total when there is only one human. The trust anchor has to be local human presence, as in the `authz:grant` typed mint, bound to the brief's auth-hash (same scope as forge-auth-hash v1: plan.id, xbrief path, concrete file_scope, acceptanceCriteria).

## Expected

- A single maintainer can land a new or widened brief and its code in one PR.
- The proof is a human-presence mint bound to the head brief's auth-hash, carried in the same PR. The human merge (`requireHumanMerge`) stays the final approval.
- CI can tell a human-minted record from a file an agent wrote. How is the open design question for the arc: candidates include a signature under a key the agent cannot read, or a mint the CI verifies against an operator-held key. A plain file in the PR is not enough.
- Without that proof, behaviour is unchanged: today's Path B, mint record PR and #6203 forge approval all keep working.
- No gate is weakened for repos that have more than one maintainer.

## Acceptance

- Given a repo with one human maintainer, when that maintainer mints approval for a widened brief and opens one PR with the brief and its code, then membership admits the PR and it merges with no separate brief or record PR.
- Given the same PR where the mint record was written by an agent (no human-presence proof), then membership rejects it with today's remediation.
- When the brief in the PR changes after the mint (auth-hash mismatch), then membership rejects it.

Refs #6203. Refs #6207.
